name: Butam
confidence_why: Butam is extinct (last speaker died 1938) and its only documentation, Futscher's 1936 notes as edited by Laufer (1959), states outright that the notes mark neither length nor stress and that no uniform word-stress rule can any longer be established, while Laufer (1950), Stebbins (2009) and Meng (2018) say nothing about Butam stress, so 'undetermined' is the only reading available and nothing contradicts it.
catalog_citation: Laufer, Carl. 1959. P. Futschers Aufzeichnungen über die Butam-Sprache (Neubritannien). Anthropos 54(1/2): 183-212.
catalog_locator: Sec. 3 'Grammatik der Butam-Sprache', subsection 'Die Silben', p. 199 (archive.org, page/n236; saved page scan)
catalog_quote: Die Silben Die Silben können lang oder kurz sein. Doch scheint es geraten, in der vorliegenden Arbeit von einer genauen Zeichensetzung abzusehen, weil solche in den vorhandenen schriftlichen Unterlagen durchgehend fehlt und auch nicht mehr nachgeholt werden kann. Aus demselben Grunde lassen sich auch keine einheitlichen Regeln für die Wortbetonung mehr festlegen. Sie wechselt häufig auf Grund euphonischer Ein- und Ausschaltungen.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.translation: Syllables can be long or short. But it seems advisable to refrain from exact diacritic marking in the present work, because such marking is absent throughout the existing written records and can no longer be supplied. For the same reason no uniform rules for word stress can be established any more. It [word stress] shifts frequently on account of euphonic insertions and elisions.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The only description of Butam explicitly declines to state a word-stress rule: Futscher's notes (1936, from the last speaker, d. 1938) did not mark length or stress and the data can no longer be checked; the compilers adds only that stress position varies often, conditioned by euphonic insertion/deletion of segments. No default position, no contrastive function, no examples with stress marks are given.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the source gives no rule to which exceptions could apply, only the remark that stress 'wechselt häufig auf Grund euphonischer Ein- und Ausschaltungen'.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is framed at word level ('Wortbetonung'); no phrase-level or citation-form discussion. Data are written notes only (no recordings); Laufer and later Meng 2018 flag the last speaker's competence as doubtful.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes Butam proper (Glottolog buta1242, no ISO code), the extinct sister language of Taulil/Tulil [tuh, taul1251] of the Gazelle Peninsula, East New Britain, from P. Otto Futscher's 1936 notes taken from the last speaker (To Vulukua, d. 1938). Not to be confused with the 'Randbutam' of southern New Ireland (Schlaginhaufen 1908; Capell 1967) whose identity with Butam Laufer leaves open. The Tulil grammar (Meng 2018) already in the catalog under taul1251 is a different language and its stress statement must not be transferred to Butam.

sources.citation: Meng, Chenxi. 2018. A grammar of Tulil. PhD thesis, La Trobe University. doi:10.26181/21857724.
sources.note: Describes Tulil (= Glottolog Taulil taul1251, the sister language), not Butam. On Butam (sec. 1.4, p.9): Laufer 1959a comprises 'around 200 words and a brief grammar sketch'; last speaker died 1938 and 'this speaker's language ability is in doubt'. Tulil stress (sec. 2.4.1) is non-contrastive, tentatively final, analysis 'very preliminary' -- not applicable to Butam.
